library_preparation_preflight.summary: I found no concrete evidence that extra setup is needed. com.couchbase.client:core-io is the low-level Couchbase SDK engine, and I did not check its published POM or documentation. I'm assuming its Netty, Jackson, reactor-core and reactive-streams dependencies come in transitively. Its public API (Core, CoreEnvironment, ConnectionString, Authenticator, retry strategies, request/response types, JSON and config parsing) can be exercised in-process without a Couchbase server. The repo has no couchbase image under allowed-docker-images. The sibling couchbase modules in the repo, metrics-micrometer and tracing-micrometer-observation, don't use one either.
risks: Tests that connect to a real Couchbase cluster would need a Couchbase Server Docker image. No couchbase image is pinned in the allow-list, so adding one would be a new entry. Prefer offline tests: build the environment, parse a connection string, decode config JSON, and construct requests and retry strategies.
Optional integrations such as micrometer and OpenTelemetry are not needed. Do not add them for core-io coverage.
